{{Top|leg}}
{{Quote|We are assembling a conclave of Naboo aristocrats who sympathize with the Resistance. One noble has sent her servant to pick up directions and clearance codes. We have arranged a wilderness rendezvous, away from prying Imperial eyes, and would like you to deliver the datadisc to the servant. Will you go?|Pooja Naberrie|<ref name="AED">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref>}}
'''Jumis''' was a servant who lived during the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Sometime following the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], [[Pooja Naberrie/Legends|Pooja Naberrie]] tasked a [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]] with delivering a [[Datacard/Legends|datadisc]] to Jumis outside the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Dee'ja Peak/Legends|Dee'ja Peak]] on [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. Although the spacer was attacked by [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]], Naberrie's mission was completed.<ref name="AED" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:TemplateCommoner.png|250px|thumb|Every possible depictions of Jumis]]
Jumis was a [[Wikipedia:Non-player character|non-player character]] in the [[2003]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars Galaxies|''Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided'']], a [[Roleplaying game|massively multiplayer online role-playing game]] developed by [[Sony]] Online Entertainment and published by [[LucasArts]], prior to its closure on [[December 15]], [[2011]].<ref name="AED" /><ref name="Shutdown">{{SonyCite|url=playerinfo|text=IMPORTANT INFORMATION ABOUT ''STAR WARS'' GALAXIES™}}</ref>

Players who performed a series of [[W:c:swg:Quest|quests]] for [[W:c:swg:Pooja Naberrie|Pooja Naberrie]] had to locate Jumis outside of [[W:c:swg:Dee'ja Peak|Dee'ja Peak]] and deliver a [[W:c:swg:Datadisc|datadisc]]. However, due to a bug, many of the NPCs in Naberrie's quests were not properly sequenced. For instance, in the quest to deliver a datadisc to Jumis, players actually encountered an individual known as [[Turon Adala]], who was supposed to appear in the following quest. The character model for Jumis likewise erroneously spawned for Naberrie's second quest, in which the player was supposed to encounter an individual named [[Herosk Bal'far]].<ref name="AED" /> According to the game files, a datadisc could not be properly delivered to Jumis, as the character (in this case Turon Adala) was not designated as a "deliver" NPC.<ref name="TRE">{{SWGcite|exp=AED|type=other|directory tree files}}</ref> Nevertheless, it was possible for the player to complete the mission and advance to the next quest. This article assumes that the content of Naberrie's quest dialogue is [[canon]] in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, and that Jumis, not Turon Adala, actually appeared during her third quest.<ref name="AED" />

Furthermore, because Jumis spawned under the generic "commoner" template, Jumis' appearance was randomized under one of a 120 possible depictions. [[Species/Legends|Species]] Jumis could appear as included [[Aqualish/Legends|Aqualish]], [[Bothan/Legends|Bothans]], [[Bith/Legends|Bith]], [[Human/Legends|Humans]], [[Rodian/Legends|Rodians]], [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshans]], [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'leks]], and [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]] of either [[Gender/Legends|gender]], and [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronians]], [[Ishi Tib/Legends|Ishi Tib]], [[Nikto/Legends|Nikto]], and [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustans]] of the male gender. Because the quest dialogue made no mention of Jumis' physical characteristics, the canonical species and gender cannot be definitively determined in the ''Star Wars'' Legends continuity.<ref name="AED" /> The questline that involved Jumis was eventually removed from the game when Pooja Naberrie was relocated to [[Theed/Legends|Theed]] as part of the newly introduced [[W:c:swg:Legacy Quest|Legacy Quest]], released as part of [[W:c:swg:Publish 25 Notes for November 15 2005|Publish 25's]] [[W:c:swg:New Game Enhancements|New Game Enhancements]] on [[November 15]], [[2005]].<ref name="AED" /><ref name="NGE">{{SonyCite|url=players/content.vm?id=64886&resource=publish|text=Publish Archive 2005}}</ref>
